summary: Before writing a module, check for an existing module, consider an action plugin, a role, or a whole collection, and design modules to do one thing well without requiring users to know every underlying API option.
questions: How do I decide if I really need to write a new module?
When should I write an action plugin instead of a module?
When does it make sense to build a collection rather than one module?
What makes a module likely to be rejected?

answer_card.title: Should you develop a module?
answer_card.answer_md:
Ask first:
1. Does a similar module exist (collections, Galaxy)?
2. Would an **action plugin** (runs on the control node) fit better?
3. Can a **role** combining existing modules do it?
4. Is it big enough to need a **collection** (new cloud, DB, network platform)?

Modules should do one thing well and not require users to know every API option; if a required parameter's legal values can't be documented, it would be rejected.
